title: Cold email sequence (B2B, small business sender)

gates.text: Truth and grounding: every prospect-specific claim (name, title, company, observation, trigger) maps to a stored source URL; every claim about the sender (results, customers, guarantees, prices) is in the confirmed facts. Gaps use [NEEDS FACT: ...]. Nothing invented or 'plausible'.

Compliance: the prospect passes jurisdiction rules (no DE/AT, UK sole traders/partnerships, or CA/AU inferred addresses); each message carries real sender name, role and company, postal address and a plain-text opt-out line; UK/EU first emails carry the Article 14 source and privacy line; Canada carries a contact method.

Deliverability and format: plain text; step 1 has no links (except the UK/EU privacy pointer in the footer), images, attachments or tracking; step 1 body 125 words or fewer and follow-ups 60 or fewer; subjects 2-5 words with no emojis, ALL CAPS or '$'; no visible merge fields or 'Hi Info'; no calendar link in cold steps.

Honesty: no fake 'Re:'/'Fwd:' on a first touch, no implied prior relationship or referral that did not happen, no false urgency or scarcity, no flattery or private-life references, no fabricated sender persona.

anchors.1: Generic pitch that could go to anyone; no observation or a vague one ('I love your website').
anchors.3: Industry-relevant but not specific to this company, or specific but not connected to a problem the sender solves.
anchors.5: One specific, sourced observation tied to a problem this company plausibly has right now; it could not be sent unchanged to a neighbouring business.

anchors.1: Feature list or jargon; the reader cannot say what is offered.
anchors.3: Value stated but vague ('grow your business', 'save time') or proof missing.
anchors.5: One concrete outcome with a number, named comparable customer (with permission) or a one-sentence mechanism from the confirmed facts.

anchors.1: Over 150 words or a wall of text; hard to read on a phone.
anchors.3: Step 1 at 90-130 words, or follow-ups over 60; readable but padded.
anchors.5: Step 1 at 50-90 words, follow-ups 25-60, 3-5 short paragraphs, plain words, scannable on a phone.

anchors.1: Several asks, or a hard meeting demand with a link.
anchors.3: A single ask but high-friction (e.g. '30-minute call this week?') in a cold step.
anchors.5: A single, low-friction, interest-based question answerable in one word, on the right rung for the step.

anchors.1: Manipulative or sycophantic, or full of AI tells and clichés ('I hope this finds you well', 'game-changer').
anchors.3: Neutral but salesy; some clichés or a stiff, templated feel.
anchors.5: Reads like a capable peer wrote it to one person: plain, respectful, specific, in the prospect's language and spelling, with no banned phrases.
2-5 plain words naming something specific to the prospect or the observation; two honest options given.

anchors.1: Follow-ups repeat the pitch or say 'bumping this'; guilt-tripping close.
anchors.3: Follow-ups vary wording but add little new; spacing or step count off the defaults without reason.
anchors.5: Steps on business days 0/3/7/14; each follow-up adds a new angle, proof or resource and stands alone; a warm, honest close-out; stops on any reply.

anchors.1: Variables with no source or fallback; a fallback that would produce a broken or false sentence; one identical body for every mailbox.
anchors.3: Fallbacks exist but some read awkwardly, or variants only swap merge fields.
anchors.5: Every variable has a stated source and a natural, true fallback; role accounts get no first name; 2-3 structural variants for multi-mailbox use; any test is one big swing measured on replies.
